clue.text: Reinvests regularly in very old part of Italy

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
one thing set in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the outer pair

blocks.note: V is the standard abbreviation for very
the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the word
O is the usual abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An investor keeps putting money back into some ancient Italian region.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'Reinvests' sit between V and O, the abbreviations for very and old.
explanation.definitionFit: The Veneto is the northeastern Italian region around Venice, so it is literally one region of that country.

clue.text: Third party deed not so good on reflection, Charlie admitted

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the letters run backwards
to be admitted is to be let inside, so one letter goes into the middle of the others

blocks.note: worse means less good
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone reckons a third-party agreement is looking worse, once a man called Charlie has been let in.
explanation.walkthrough: WORSE written backwards gives ESROW, and C is slipped in after the first two letters to make ESCROW.
explanation.definitionFit: An escrow is a bond or document held by an independent party until agreed conditions are met, a legal arrangement involving outsiders.

clue.text: Bad weather near The Potteries might produce this

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the letters are spoilt into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weather forecast suggests storms around Stoke-on-Trent could lead to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The Potteries is the area around Stoke-on-Trent in Staffordshire, England, historically the heart of British ceramics making. 'Bad weather' reads as the cause, but the eleven letters of weather and near are the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthenware is fired clay pottery, exactly the kind of goods the Staffordshire factories turned out for centuries.

clue.text: Ruling class roll cigars after tossing wrappings on Cape hotel lobby, finally

indicators.note: throwing away the wrappers removes the outside, so each word loses its first and last letters
finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the word with its outer letters removed
the word with its outer letters removed
C is the map abbreviation for cape
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Members of the elite unwrap and roll cigars in the lobby of a hotel on the Cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' looks like a verb about making cigars, but it is a second word to be unwrapped. The trimmed words OL and IGAR are followed by C, H and the Y ending lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarchy is government by a small privileged group, so the term names that ruling elite collectively.

clue.text: Premium, as the adverts showcasing The Times for one

indicators.note: to showcase is to put on display, so the run of letters is on view within the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, two whole words and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A newspaper charges top rates, much as its adverts boast about the paper itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times is the newspaper this puzzle appears in; its name in large type across the top of the front page is the masthead.
explanation.definitionFit: A masthead is the title banner printed at the top of a newspaper's front page, and The Times nameplate is one such banner.

clue.text: Vermin bothered Athene at first, being a goddess

indicators.note: being bothered means being disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order
at first points to the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: Pests pestered the Greek goddess Athene.
explanation.walkthrough: Athene is used for her initial only, though fittingly she is the Greek counterpart of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerva is the Roman goddess of wisdom, crafts and war, so she is one of the classical deities.

clue.text: Muscle function beginning to weaken

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so just that one is kept

blocks.note: sine is a trigonometric function
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A body's muscles start to lose their strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' sounds biological here, but it is the mathematical sense, a trig ratio.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew means a tendon, and by extension muscular strength or brawn, so it stands for muscle in the loose sense.

clue.text: Embrace university in Wells?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the single letter goes between the others

blocks.note: the initials of the novelist H. G. Wells
U is the usual abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the cathedral city of Wells has a university to welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Wells looks like the small English cathedral city, but the question mark flags the author of The War of the Worlds, whose initials are HG.
explanation.definitionFit: To hug and to embrace both mean holding someone tightly in your arms, a direct synonym pair.

clue.text: Selflessness is founded in key spirit

indicators.note: something founded in a place is set down within it, so the small word goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A moral claim that unselfishness rests on a crucial inner quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key spirit' reads as an essential attitude, but it is a keyboard key followed by a drink, with IS placed inside the rum.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is concern for the wellbeing of others above oneself, a precise synonym for unselfish behaviour.

clue.text: Small firm working to absorb a measure of inflation which can be lethal

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a noun

indicators.note: to absorb something is to soak it up and take it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
Co is short for company
the Retail Prices Index, a UK inflation figure
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A small business struggles to cope with inflation, which could finish it off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Retail Prices Index is a British inflation figure; 'working' is the familiar crossword sense of switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: Some scorpion species carry a venomous sting strong enough to kill a person, so the creature fits a description of deadly things.

clue.text: Deny wife’s escaped from prison once

indicators.note: whatever has escaped is no longer there, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: Newgate was a notorious London jail, closed in 1902
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to admit that his wife broke out of an old jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Newgate was a famous London prison, long demolished, hence 'once'; take W out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate a statement is to contradict or nullify it, which matches refusing to accept something as true.

clue.text: Tease upper-class Head of Accounts who’s up before Judges

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: to josh is to tease playfully
U is the old label for upper-class usage
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a posh head of finance who has to appear before the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up before Judges' suggests a court appearance, but it means the Bible book placed immediately before the Book of Judges.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament the Book of Joshua comes directly ahead of the Book of Judges in canonical order.

clue.text: Bloody large swig knocked back — one might get hammered!

indicators.note: something knocked back is driven the other way, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: bloody meat is raw
L is the abbreviation for large
a gulp is a big swallow of drink

explanation.surface: Downing a large drink in one go is a good way to end up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammered means drunk in British slang, the surface reading; a Rawlplug is the British trade name for a plastic wall plug, tapped into a drilled hole with a hammer before a screw goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall plug is commonly knocked into its hole with a hammer, so it is an item that literally gets struck.

clue.text: GI teleports wicked ghost

indicators.note: something wicked is twisted or perverse, so these letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sci-fi scene where an evil spirit beams an American soldier away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' looks like it describes the ghost, but it is the signal to rearrange the eleven letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A poltergeist is a noisy, mischievous spirit said to move objects, which is one kind of ghost.

clue.text: Loudly panned top celebs framing poor bum, a vagrant sleeper?

indicators.note: loudly means spoken out, so the word is taken for its sound rather than its spelling
something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are rearranged
a frame goes round a picture, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: to pan a show is to knock it, criticise it harshly
the A-list are the most famous celebrities
taken as written

explanation.surface: Critics savaged famous people for sheltering a down-and-out who sleeps rough.
explanation.walkthrough: A vagrant here is a wanderer and the sleeper wanders while asleep; the question mark marks that playful reading. Bum is slang for a tramp, adding to the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A noctambulist is a sleepwalker, someone who roams about at night while not awake, from Latin nox and ambulare.

clue.text: Specialist field being security, one’s descending on N Scottish town

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece coming down onto another sits directly above it

blocks.note: bail is money pledged as security for a defendant's return
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's means 'one is'
Wick is a town in Caithness in the far north of Scotland

explanation.surface: A security expert swoops down on a town in northern Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Wick is a small town on the Caithness coast at the northern tip of mainland Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Bailiwick originally meant a bailiff's district and is now used for a person's own area of expertise or interest.

clue.text: Overbearing tail coat lined with titanium

indicators.note: a lining sits inside a garment, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to tail and to dog both mean to follow closely
a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh
Ti is the chemical symbol for titanium

explanation.surface: A domineering figure in a tailcoat lined with metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail coat' reads as formal evening wear, but the two words split: tail is a verb meaning follow, coat is a mac.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogmatic people assert their opinions as unquestionable truth, which comes across as arrogant and domineering.

clue.text: Motor on, in gear: tyre needs changing

indicators.note: something that needs changing must be altered, so these letters take a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A garage diagnosis: the car runs in gear but a tyre must be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: Motor looks like the British word for a car in the surface, but it is the definition of a type of engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotary engine is an internal combustion engine with a spinning rotor instead of pistons, one kind of motor.

clue.text: Justice after English blokes upset relative

indicators.note: something upset is turned over, so in a down entry the letters read upwards
after says that one piece follows the other in the finished word

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
blokes is British slang for men
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A relative is angry at a group of Englishmen and demands justice.
explanation.walkthrough: Blokes is everyday British slang for men. In a down entry 'upset' turns the letters upside down, which reads as a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis is retributive justice, the inescapable punishment named after the Greek goddess of vengeance.

clue.text: Blast drunken revelry where whiskey is confiscated

indicators.note: what is confiscated is taken away, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: wassail is festive drinking and carousing
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone curses a boozy party where the whiskey is taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: Whiskey reads as the drink, fitting the party, but it is the radio code word for W.
explanation.definitionFit: To blast someone is to attack them fiercely, especially in words, which is what assail means too.

clue.text: Briefly endanger, with little hesitation, supreme power

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: imperil means endanger; here it is shortened
um is a small sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A dictator puts absolute authority at risk for a moment, with hardly a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' seems to say how long the danger lasts, but it trims the end off a synonym for endanger.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperium is Latin for command and denotes absolute authority, the highest power of a ruler or state.

clue.text: Perfectly formed proposal put forward Liberal

indicators.note: put forward means placed in front, so this piece comes first in the down entry

blocks.note: an idea is a suggestion or proposal
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician advances a neatly crafted proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put forward' reads as proposing a motion, but it tells you the proposal goes in front of the party letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal describes something exactly as it should be, without flaw, matching the sense of flawless in shape.

clue.text: Take broadcast with good humour

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard rather than read, so the phrase counts for its sound

blocks.note: done in jest is done playfully, with good humour

explanation.surface: Accept a radio programme in good spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take broadcast' looks like a recording instruction, but take is the definition and broadcast tells you to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or medicine into the body, so take works in the swallowing sense.

clue.text: Plain action of speaker

indicators.note: what comes from a speaker is heard, so the word is taken for how it is pronounced

blocks.note: a step is an action or measure taken

explanation.surface: A plain account of what a public speaker did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' wants to be an adjective for straightforward; it is the noun for flat grassland. A step, as in 'the next step', is an action.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassy flatland, as in Russia or Central Asia, which is a plain in the geographic sense.

clue.text: Highly acidic character

blocks.note: surface reading: a person with a sharp, caustic temperament
setter's reading: a Greek letter that reads as the acidity scale followed by the Roman numeral one, a very acidic value

explanation.walkthrough: pH measures acidity, and the lower the number the stronger the acid, so pH 1 is very acidic; write the 1 as I to get PHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet, and crosswords often use character to mean a written letter.

clue.text: Steel instrument with built-in retro microphone

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the letters run the other way
something built in is fitted inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: mic is short for microphone
a sitar is an Indian stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A steel guitar fitted with an old-fashioned pickup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steel instrument' reads as a steel guitar, but steel alone is the definition, in its old sense of a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel is a literary word for a sword, and a scimitar is a curved oriental sword.

clue.text: Famous Greek Conservative fell in the flipping Med!

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters run backwards
to be in something is to be inside it, so these pieces go within the other

blocks.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a fell is a hill or upland in northern England

explanation.surface: A well-known Greek Tory tumbled into the blasted Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a past tense, but it is the northern English noun for a hill. The Med is a sea, turned round to AES around C and HILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the celebrated hero of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad, among the best-known figures of Greek legend.

clue.text: Space formed by police where things are at boiling point?

definitions.text: where things are at boiling point?

blocks.note: first meaning: a cordon in which police hem in protesters

blocks.clueFragment: where things are at boiling point?
blocks.note: second meaning: the household appliance in which water boils

explanation.walkthrough: Kettling is a British police tactic of corralling demonstrators in a confined area; the question mark lets 'boiling point' hint at tempers in that crowd too.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a police containment cordon around a crowd and the vessel used for heating water.
